CmdIdent.description: An identifier: non-empty, one line, NFC, without leading or trailing white space (doc 05 §3.2).

CmdMlText.description: Multilingual text: a neutral string, or an object keyed by canonical BCP 47 tags in ascending order with non-empty string values (doc 05 §3.2).

CmdUuid.description: A lower-case hyphenated UUID naming a record (doc 05 §3.2).

Dec3.description: A canonical decimal string: at most three fraction digits, no trailing fraction zeros, no leading zeros, no plus sign, no "-0", no exponent, no white space, no unit (doc 05 §3.2). The pattern bounds the integer part to 16 digits; the exact i64 range of the thousandths (about 9.2 x 10^15) is checked by the reader.

Ident.description: An identifier: non-empty, one line (no control character U+0000 to U+001F or U+007F to U+009F), without leading or trailing white space (the Unicode White_Space set); interior spaces are allowed (doc 05 §3.2). JSON Schema cannot express Unicode Normalization Form C; the reader rejects non-NFC text.

LevelRole.description: The role of a terminal level.

LevelSpec.description: One level of a multi-level terminal.

PartRef.description: A part on a device (doc 03 §7): the embedded copy and an optional part variant (FR-PRT-003).

copy.description: The copy ID of the embedded part, `v5(NS_LIBCOPY, library ‖ item)`.

variant.description: A variant key of the part.

PartUse.description: A part use on a device (ADR-0006): the part and its quantity in the part's order unit.

qty.description: The quantity in the part's order unit (pieces, metres, sets).

designation.description: The designation, unique within the strip.

seq.description: The drawn and mounting order; default one more than the highest in the strip.

description:
`terminal.insert`: new terminals of a strip at a position, the following terminals moved up (WP-S2.07 §5.1, D4).

Let s be the `seq` of `before` (absent: one more than the strip's highest `seq`, or 1 for an empty strip) and n
the number of terminals. In one transaction every terminal of the strip with `seq ≥ s` gets `seq + n` (its tag
and designation stay), every group bound (`from_seq`, `to_seq`) and every accessory `after_seq` at or above s is
raised by n, and the new terminals are inserted as `terminal.add` inserts them, with `seq` s, s + 1, … in list
order and `parts` on each. Rejected: the strip is not a device with the strip aspect; `before` is not a terminal of
the strip; no terminal; a spec with `seq`; a designation already used in the strip or twice in the list; a
sequence number beyond 4294967295. A missing strip, `before`, function definition or part copy is `NotFound`.
Cost Interactive. Outcome: the first new terminal device.

before.description: The terminal of the strip the new terminals go before; absent or null: after the last terminal.

parts.description: The part uses each new terminal gets.

terminals.description:
The terminals, at least one, in mounting order; their position follows from `before`, so `seq` is not
allowed.
